newsitem.title: USA: New York lawmakers reject casino gambling.
newsitem.headline: New York lawmakers reject casino gambling.

text.p: New York lawmakers on Tuesday rejected a bill that would have legalised casino gambling in the state, effectively killing the issue for this year.
The state Senate voted 41-19 against the bill which, if it had passed, would have put the question of casino gambling before voters in November in a statewide referendum.
"The bill is dead for this year and will not be reconsidered," said a spokesman for Republican Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno.
The vote came after four hours of debate.
The casino gambling had been proposed for four areas in the state, including the Catskill Mountains resort area and the world-famous Niagara Falls.
Gambling supporters had argued that the measure could win away billions of dollars from the casino gambling industries in New Jersey and Connecticut.

The opposition included church groups, environmentalists and the state's thoroughbred horse racing industry. Opponents claimed other states that have legalised casino gambling have seen little economic gain but have paid for considerably larger police forces and more social services.
Currently casino gambling in New York is only permitted at Turning Stone, which is land belonging to the Oneida Indians.
